transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Huang (Redwood SE), Ruth Delgado (CTO - Paloma), Evan Brooks (ML Eng), Maya Singh (SRE)

Summary:
Quick check-in on week 3 POC results: throughput and cost figures, caching wins observed, and tuning plan for batching vs latency. Agreement to run a longer stability run and share detailed traces.

Topics: tokens/sec per dollar, prefix/K V cache savings, batching impact on p95 latency, dataset/trace handoff, SOC2 + VPC questions.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: results, tuning notes, and next steps. lena and i will run through the numbers we sent this morning.
[00:18] Ruth: cool, thanks. we wanna make sure the economics line up before we escalate to infra.
[00:23] Lena: alright, jumping in — we ran the same 3 workloads you sent over: short Q/A, summarization, and multi-turn routing. baseline was hosted small model variant (rwd-small-2) and a quantized dedicated instance.
[00:38] Evan: just to clarify, the sample traces had an average prompt length of ~48 tokens, right? there was a spike with one of the summarization prompts at 420 tokens which skewed the avg.
[00:46] Lena: yeah, that long one is the outlier; median prompt length is 32 tokens. we calculated tokens per second and tokens per dollar.
[00:54] Lena: baseline hosted: about 1,900 tokens/sec across the cluster for the summarization workload, cost ~ $1.12 per 1k requests (note: the sheet has the broken-down per-token cost). dedicated quantized run: 3,400 tokens/sec and unit cost per million tokens roughly 0.74 — so about 2.6x throughput at 35% lower per-token cost in steady state.
[01:20] Maya: hmm okay. but what about latency — p95 numbers? throughput's great but we can't have user-facing tails.
[01:27] Lena: good call. p95 for hosted was 280ms for short Q/A, 780ms for summarization. dedicated with batching (bs=8) gave 430ms median for summarization and p95 ~1.1s. so batching lifts throughput but increases tail.
[01:46] Samir: that's the classic tradeoff. tokens/sec per dollar went up with batching but p95 degraded. for the routing microservice, we suggested a hybrid: small batch sizes (bs=4) plus aggressive prefix caching for repeated contexts.
[02:00] Ruth: you mentioned prefix caching — how big were the savings? numbers please.
[02:05] Lena: with prefix caching enabled (we warm cache on the initial anchor prompts), we saw token reductions of 45% on the short Q/A workload and 28% on summarization. effectively the observed tokens-per-invocation dropped, which converts to roughly 38% lower cost per successful request in the short Q/A pattern.
[02:26] Evan: is that true caching or K V cache reuse? i'm asking because our prompts include dynamic user metadata which can break naive prefix caching.
[02:36] Lena: yeah sorry — a mix. our runtime has both prefix-level caching and KV cache reuse for autoregressive states. for repeated system prompts and boilerplate, prefix caching hits are high. for user-specific tags we rely on partial-match strategy which still saved ~20%. the transcript in the sheet shows some mis-labeled "K V cash" in the auto notes, haha.
[02:58] Samir: and important to flag — caching savings scale with request locality. during our synthetic test where 60% of requests used the same system prompt, savings were max; in a full fanout scenario savings will be lower.
[03:13] Maya: about batching tradeoffs — can we quantify tokens/sec per dollar at different batch sizes? we need a recommendation for production.
[03:20] Lena: sure. quick numbers from the sweep: bs=1 tokens/sec 3,400 (dedicated), cost per M tokens $0.74; bs=4 tokens/sec 4,200 cost effective improvement ~ +18% but p95 increased by ~18%; bs=8 tokens/sec 5,200 but p95 jumped by ~45% from baseline; bs=16 tokens/sec 5,600 but p95 unacceptable for interactive (p95 > 2s). net tokens/sec per dollar peaked at bs=8 for throughput-heavy pipelines but bs=4 was the best compromise for sub-second p95 in most cases.
[03:58] Ruth: okay so for our routing calls (user-facing) we should default bs=4 and raise to 8 during background batch windows.
[04:06] Evan: can we autoscale batch size based on queue depth and time budget?
[04:10] Lena: yes the Redwood runtime supports dynamic batching policies: max latency threshold, adaptive bucket sizing. we can apply a policy like target p95 < 900ms then cap batch size to 4, otherwise allow 8 for non-interactive flows.
[04:24] Ruth: good. whats the expected tokens per dollar if we enable 48h stability run and 60% cache locality?
[04:31] Lena: with those parameters our model of projects tokens per dollar improvement of ~32% over baseline hosted. so if baseline was $X per million tokens, you'd drop to ~0.68X given warm caches and bs=4 mixing. note this is sensitive to cache hit rate and long prompt tail.
[04:49] Samir: real-world note — we saw one run where an unseen long-context chat (1.2k tokens) ballooned cost 4x for that invocation. we flagged that and recommended a hard max prompt length enforcement or summary compaction pre-step.
[05:03] Evan: we will likely do compaction on the client side but want to log how often it happens. i'll provide traces.
[05:09] [05:12] Lena: quick question from paloma — security and private deployment concerns?
[05:15] Ruth: yes, our legal requires VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for any PII workloads within 90 days of go-live.
[05:23] Samir: we can do Redwood Private with VPC and KMS integrations — showing the SOC2 docs should help. i'll push the SOC2 summary and the private deployment checklist after this call.
[05:33] Maya: for network architecture, do you support transit gateway or do we need a VPN tunnel for on-prem?
[05:38] Lena: both supported, we've done TGW peering with cloud providers and IPSec VPN for on-prem. there may be egress configuration steps for audit logging which we can share.
[05:48] [05:55] Ruth: cool. on the economics side, we need the full spreadsheet with per-route breakdowns (routing vs summarization vs storage calls). can you slice by route and show projected monthly spend at 1M and 10M monthly active users?
[06:06] Samir: yes we'll provide per-route projections. we'll also include two scenarios: conservative (low cache locality) and optimistic (60% cache locality).
[06:15] Evan: quick nit — in your sheet earlier there was a column labeled "tokens/sec/$" which seemed to be tokens per second normalized by cost; can you clarify units?
[06:23] Lena: sure — that's tokens rendered per dollar per second normalized to the instance footprint. it's a bit wonky phrasing, we'll rename it to "tokens per dollar (steady-state)" and add a note.
[06:33] Ruth: one more ask — can we run a pilot with redwood dedicated for 2 weeks with configurable batch policies so we can see production tail behavior?
[06:41] Samir: yes we can do a timeboxed dedicated pilot; usual ask is a short contract and some commit for capacity. we'll draft options: 2-week dedicated eval or longer reserved trial.
[06:50] Maya: cost for the dedicated eval?
[06:52] Samir: short eval is discounted; we'll include exact numbers in the pricing doc. expectation is you only pay for consumed tokens and a small infra fee for reserved instances during the window.
[06:59] [07:05] Lena: operational items — we recommend three runs for data: 1) 24h synthetic sweep to validate batch sweep numbers, 2) 48-72h stability run with 60% warm cache pattern, 3) a mixed production-shaped run with random long-tail prompts to validate compaction strategy.
[07:24] Ruth: agreed. final question — competitors? we've seen price/perf numbers from Anthropic and Vertex that look similar. any reason to pick Redwood for infra?
[07:33] Samir: short answer: the unified runtime + caching primitives + deterministic rollouts. also our console gives token-level cost per route which helps you find regressions quickly. we'll include comparative benchmark notes.
[07:45] Evan: can you run a short A/B during the dedicated trial where half traffic goes to Anthropic and half to Redwood for perf comparison?
[07:52] Samir: technically yes — routing policy can split and we can add canary rules. may need NDA with the other provider but for your eval we can simulate similar request patterns.
[08:01] Lena: any final blockers?
[08:03] Ruth: timeline — we need infra decision in 3 weeks. if the dedicated trial shows the p95 improvement at bs=4 and caching holds, we'll move forward.
[08:11] Samir: great, recap of next steps: Samir will send pricing + SOC2 + private checklist by 2026-02-23; Lena will run batch sweep and cache-enabled benchmark and share logs by 2026-02-24; Evan will provide production traces by 2026-02-25; Paloma to confirm dedicated trial window by 2026-02-27.
[08:29] Ruth: thanks all, that works.
[08:32] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread and post the updated spreadsheet. bye.
